text: Hello everyone, I'm Grace Chu.We're going to have a reading lesson today.Let's get our worksheet, our notebook, and our pens ready.Today, we're going to learn a reading strategy identifying the main idea.Let's start our lesson.A good reader knows how to identify the main idea in a text.What's the main idea?It is the most important point in a text.It is usually supported by most of the information in the text.Our teachers use certain types of questions to test if we are good at finding the main ideas.This is the first task on your worksheet.Take a moment to take the questions about main ideas.Yes, they are.Number one, what is the passage mainly about?Number two, what is the topic of the text?And number six, what would be the best title of the story?These are questions about main ideas.These questions ask us to find out about the topic, the title, and the message of the text.They are all related to the main ideas.Can you think of some other questions about the main idea of the text?For example, what can you learn from the passage?What does the writer want to tell us?Or what does this article mainly suggest?If we can find the main idea the writer wants to tell us, we can better understand the whole passage.Now, where is the main idea?Let's take a look at some paragraphs in task two on our worksheet.Find task two.Here's example one.Can you find the main idea?Have you found the main idea?It's right at the beginning of this paragraph.So, the writer wants to tell us that laughter is the best medicine.The sentence which tells us the main idea is called a topic sentence.Many writers like to put topic sentence at the beginning of their paragraph or their passage.Then they go on to use examples or explanations to support their topic sentence.In this case, you can see the writer quotes other people's findings.It is said that if you laugh every day, you'll forget your worries.You'll live better and then you can live longer.Some doctors even recommend laughter to their patients for their illnesses.So, here every sentence supports the main idea.It shows laughter is really the best medicine.It's very useful.As you can see, all the four sentences here support the topic sentence.Laughter is the best medicine.Let's move on to the second example.Can you also find and then underline the topic sentence in this paragraph?So, where is the topic sentence in the second example?This time, we can find the topic sentence at the end of the paragraph.The first sentence tells us one example.Within seconds means very fast.People all over the world can know which team wins in a big sports game.And the second and third sentences tell us another example.When a disaster happens, news will spread quickly because we have cameras,radios, TVs, newspapers and social apps like WeChat or Facebook.And then people from faraway countries will come to help by car, train or even plane.So, here it says, within hours, help is on the way.So, we are clear that the whole paragraph has only one idea supported by two examples.That is, because of modern technology, information travels fast.Very often, the writer will give the main idea at the beginning and then repeat the main idea at the end.The writer will give the main idea at the beginning and then repeat the main idea at the end of the passage by using a different sentence pattern.Do you remember this passage we learned in grade 8?Can you find the topic sentence?Here is the topic sentence, also the main idea.Everyone today uses electricity in one way or another.Electricity is very useful here.And at the end of the passage, the writer again tells us his main idea.Indeed, electricity finds as much work to do in the countryside as it does in the cities.This is called a concluding sentence.The second and third paragraphs develop the main idea in our cities and also in our countryside.And it shows that electricity works everywhere.That's the topic of the whole passage, the title of the whole passage.Why am I think it's so easy to find the main idea?No, not every time.Sometimes the writer thinks we readers are smart enough to conclude the main idea ourselves.For example, the next paragraph in task 2 is more challenging.Now take out your worksheet.Take a look at the third paragraph.This time we need to read through the sentences to find details to support the main idea.See dishes are dirty.There are floors to sweep and clothes to wash, fold and put away.Tiles are smelly and furniture needs to be dusted and repaired.All those details support this one idea that's called a lot of housework needs to be done.So all of these are clues to help us find the main idea.A lot of housework needs to be done in this house.Remember here, the main idea needs to be supported by most of the details in the text.We can also use the features of the passage to help us find the main idea more quickly.They are called text features.In this passage, we can first look at the heading, the picture, the introduction, the subtitles first.These are all text features to show us this passage is about different fairs and festivals in Colorado this summer.Please read example 5 in task 2 and find the answer to this exercise, the main idea of this list.Okay, is it easy to help us find the main idea with these text features and also these verbal phrases?For example, learn about, enjoy, take part in, observe, hear, play with and try.We can see that they all talk about different activities.So in this way, we can find the main idea more quickly.Here is the answer.Have you got it?It's about activities to enjoy this summer in Colorado, USA.After completing task 2, can we summarize some useful ways to help us identify the main ideas?Here are some tips.You can take down some notes on your worksheet.We can look for the first sentence or the first paragraph of the text.The last sentence or the last paragraph of the text.Clue words repeated in the text.These are supporting details for the main idea.And pay attention to text features, for example, titles, subtitles, introductions, pictures, etc.Always remember the main idea needs to be supported by most of the details in the text.Now are you ready for some practice?Find task 4 on your worksheet.Use the tips to help you find the main ideas.Let's start.It seems we can't find a clear topic sentence in this paragraph.Let's look for clue words or supporting details.We find these two words, typhoon and tornado, are repeated in the paragraph several times.And the writer also uses but, however, while to show us they are different.For example, a typhoon may bring a lot of rain, but a tornado won't.So we can conclude the purpose of this passage is to tell us that a typhoon and a tornado are different.Let's try another one.Please work out the answer by yourself first.Here we have four choices.Let's see if they are supported by most of the details.Choice A, people enjoy watching seahorses.It has only one supporting detail.That's the last sentence in the paragraph.The seahorse is a popular fish for an aquarium.And for choice B, the seahorse is not a horse but a fish.We can find the sentence here, but in the paragraph, the writer doesn't explain why it's a fish instead of a horse.So no more supporting details.Choice C, the seahorse behaves very strangely is only supported by one sentence in the paragraph.It swims upright.No more other details.However, the first and second sentences show the seahorse looks strange.And the third sentence shows it behaves strangely.So we have lots of details to support the last choice, D.So here is our answer.The main idea is choice D, the seahorse is a strange fish.Okay, let's try another one on a worksheet.Work on your own first.Now let's check the answers.In the first sentence and second sentence, you can find that the supermarkets have two different ways to attract customers.They either spray a cake smell into the air or they spray the fresh smell of baking bread.And in the next two sentences, we can see that these smells attract people.They make people's mouth water.So we have all these details to support this main idea, how people are attracted to bakery counters.So have you found the answer?Now let's use a passage and examination paper to test ourselves.Take a moment to find the main idea yourself.So did you use the tips you learned today?Some students might go for choice C.However, it's hard to find many details to show the writer or his family have received lots of love from others in this passage.Let's take another look at the first paragraph.We can find the writer likes to sell things.I became very interested in shopping.I wanted to sell something.I enjoy myself by selling things on my dad's account.All of those details show us that the writer likes to sell things.The next paragraph, continue to talk about how he was good at buying and selling and even helped a lady by helping her sell her items.In the last paragraph, the writer again says that his skill, here means his skill as a good businessman, could be used to help others in need.Therefore, the best title should be a helpful skill.That's choice D.Sometimes, in a close test, we are also asked to identify the main idea.Let's move on to the last task, task 5.In this task, you are asked to find the name of the festival the writer is introducing.Please use the tips to find the answer.Okay, let's check the answer.First, let's pay attention to the test features like the title, a festival to celebrate spring, and the subtitle, holy in India.We can see the festival is in India, and it's a festival to celebrate the season spring.Then we look for clue words repeated in this passage.We found people use colourful paints.People throw buckets of paint at each other.As nature blooms into the colours of spring, so do people of India.So here it means that the people of India are all dressed in beautiful clothes, and because of the paint, their clothes are very colourful.So all of these details show us, here's the answer.It's the festival of colours.Holi is also known as the festival of colours.In Hindi, the official language used in India, holy means colour.Well done, everyone.We've successfully completed five tasks.Let's review what we've learned today.What is the main idea?It's the most important point the writer wants to tell us in the text, usually supported by most of the details in the text.How to identify the main idea?We can look at the beginning and ending of the text, or we can use text features to help us, and look for clue words or supporting details in the text.Congratulations.We're almost at the end of our lesson.Here is our today's homework.Number one, review what you've learned in today's lesson.Number two, finish the exercises on the homework sheet by using the tips given today.Remember, we're one step closer to becoming a better reader today.See you next time.
